fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is generic thermomechanical processing, whereas the relevant control method is temperature-dependent annealing at 1100–1300 °C followed by water quenching.
The hypothesis introduces strain rate and deformation amount even though these were not variables in the phase-evolution experiment.
It misses the central mechanism: cooling-induced spinodal separation of BCC into compositionally distinct products followed by Ni–Al-rich B2 ordering and reciprocal BCC/B2 nanostructure formation.
The stated initial state and baseline do not match the homogenized, hot-forged, re-homogenized alloy or the 1100 °C annealed-and-quenched comparison condition.
It does not predict the observed increase in BCC fraction, B2 precipitation, and hardness with increasing annealing temperature.
explanation: The response recognizes only the broad idea that processing can alter phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs. It does not reconstruct the studied method, its temperature and quenching conditions, or why it works. The proposed diffusion, dislocation, and recrystallization mechanism is generic and omits the experimentally inferred spinodal-decomposition and ordering pathway. Its outcome, limits, and falsification test are too broad to distinguish the reported hypothesis, and no supporting evidence is supplied.
